column20: What went wrong and why? - "a service engineer initiated the switch to move to automatic keys ... immediately causing the key to roll over"
column21: What happened? - "failures when requesting managed identity tokens or performing management operations for managed identities in the Australia East region"
column22: What happened? - "All identities in this region were subject to impact"; requests to the failover pair Australia Southeast also failed
column23: What happened? - "in the Australia East region, between 00:55 UTC and 06:28 UTC on 12 July 2024"
column24: How did we respond? - "all zones in Australia East were impacted - and requests to the failover pair, Australia Southeast, were also failing"
column25: How did we respond? - "our standard mitigation playbook is to perform a failover to a different zone or region. However, in this case..." and "we attempted several mitigation steps ... After these were not effective"
column26: What went wrong and why? - "Our internal deployment tooling reported a successful deployment and did not clearly show that these regions were still pinned to the older version"
column27: How can customers make incidents like this less impactful? - "customers who were able to fail out of Australia East would have been able to mitigate their impact" (supports V8b only)
column28: V1 coded config_change for the key-rollover switch that invalidated the in-use key, with the pinned older service build as secondary; V8a/V8c unclear because the report says nothing about tenant isolation or a pre-tested local fallback.
